sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, Episode 14, Interface Description Languages.
sentences.zh: Programming Throwdown，第 14 期，接口描述语言。

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: 开始吧，Jason。

sentences.en: Hey, so my Twitter and Facebook account got hijacked.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我的 Twitter 和 Facebook 账号被劫持了。

sentences.en: No!
sentences.zh: 不会吧！

sentences.en: It was not good times.
sentences.zh: 那段日子可真不好过。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I spent a significant amount of time today cleaning up, you know, tweets and posts that I didn't make.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我今天花了不少时间清理那些我根本没发过的推文和帖子。

sentences.en: But they're archived forever somewhere.
sentences.zh: 但它们永远被存档在某个地方了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, now, coincidentally, Facebook is sending me ads for Russian models.
sentences.zh: 现在倒好，Facebook 竟然给我推送俄罗斯模特的广告。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: So, was it better or worse than losing a wallet?
sentences.zh: 那么，这比丢钱包更糟糕还是稍微好点？

sentences.en: Or have you ever lost a wallet before?
sentences.zh: 或者说你以前丢过钱包吗？

sentences.en: No, I've never lost a wallet.
sentences.zh: 没有，我从没丢过钱包。

sentences.en: I did lose my keys, but I lost them actually in the bottom of a lake.
sentences.zh: 我倒是丢过钥匙，不过我是把它们掉进湖底了。

sentences.en: So, I kind of figured that they weren't coming back and no one was finding them.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就想，它们肯定找不回来了，也没人会捡到。

sentences.en: So, one day somebody will drive away with your car after finding keys in the bottom of a lake.
sentences.zh: 搞不好哪天有人在湖底捡到钥匙，直接把你的车开走了。

sentences.en: Yeah, especially now.
sentences.zh: 是啊，尤其是现在。

sentences.en: But, yeah, basically, you know, we talked about KeePass, which is an awesome program.
sentences.zh: 不过，基本上我们之前聊过 KeePass，那是个很棒的程序。

sentences.en: Highly recommend, especially now.
sentences.zh: 强烈推荐，尤其是现在。

sentences.en: Highly recommend everyone use it.
sentences.zh: 强烈建议每个人都用它。

sentences.en: But I wasn't using KeePass, you know, for a while, especially before the show.
sentences.zh: 但我有一段时间没用 KeePass 了，特别是在节目开始前的那阵子。

sentences.en: And so, I had, like, a default password that I used for things that I didn't really care about, like, Twitter and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以我给那些不太在意的网站，比如 Twitter 和 Facebook，设了一个默认密码。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it was just completely alpha characters.
sentences.zh: 对，而且全是字母。

sentences.en: It wasn't, you know, numeric or anything.
sentences.zh: 不是数字什么的。

sentences.en: And plus, I used the same password for, like, basically everything I didn't care about.
sentences.zh: 再加上我基本上所有不在意的账号都用同一个密码。

sentences.en: Like, anytime I had to sign up for anything.
sentences.zh: 就是任何时候需要注册什么东西时都用那个。

sentences.en: And so, invariably, you know, somebody, you know, didn't store my password securely and, you know, got leaked out and associated my email and everything.
sentences.zh: 结果可想而知，有人没能安全存储我的密码，导致密码泄露，还关联了我的邮箱等等。

sentences.en: And so, somebody just went through and systematically logged into everything that they could get into with that password.
sentences.zh: 于是，有人就顺藤摸瓜，用那个密码系统性地登录了所有他们能进的账号。

sentences.en: So, it turned out you were in Europe asking for money after being kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 所以结果就是，你在欧洲被人绑架了，还在网上到处要钱。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, I, the way I found out was kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 我发现这件事的过程还挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I got an email from Facebook saying someone with an IP address they traced to Japan, you know, logged in successfully as me to Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我收到 Facebook 的邮件，说有人通过追踪到的日本 IP 地址，成功登录了我的 Facebook 账号。

sentences.en: And so, that kind of tipped me off.
sentences.zh: 这给我提了个醒。

sentences.en: And so, then I went and sure enough, there were all these tweets on Twitter and Facebook posts that I didn't make and I had to clean all that up.
sentences.zh: 然后我去看了一下，果然，Twitter 和 Facebook 上全是那些我没发过的推文和帖子，我不得不把它们全清理掉。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Did anybody else let you know?
sentences.zh: 有其他人提醒你吗？

sentences.en: Like, did any of your friends see what was going on?
sentences.zh: 比如你的朋友有没有发现什么异常？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: So, interestingly, this all happened really quickly.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这一切发生得非常快。

sentences.en: So, basically, you know, the tweets started, I would say, like, eight hours before I found out.
sentences.zh: 基本上，那些推文大概是在我发现前八个小时开始发的。

sentences.en: So, you know, the person, like, hadn't had enough time for it really to propagate to any of my friends or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 所以那个人还没来得及让这些信息传播到我的朋友那里。

sentences.en: And the Facebook posts were even more recent than that.
sentences.zh: Facebook 的帖子就更近了。

sentences.en: So, they didn't change their password, though?
sentences.zh: 不过他们没改你的密码吗？

sentences.en: Because that would have been bad because the recovery for your password would have been your email, which you then also didn't have access to.
sentences.zh: 因为如果改了就麻烦了，毕竟密码找回功能依赖的是你的邮箱，而你当时也无法访问那个邮箱。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 确实，你说得对。

sentences.en: Yeah, this could have been a disaster.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这本可能演变成一场灾难。

sentences.en: Actually, it's interesting you mention that because my co-worker's uncle's Yahoo account got hacked, hijacked.
sentences.zh: 其实你提到这个很有意思，我同事的叔叔的雅虎账号就被黑了，被劫持了。

sentences.en: And they actually changed the, you know, forgot password, like, the backup email.
sentences.zh: 那些黑客甚至改了他的“忘记密码”备用邮箱。

sentences.en: They changed that to an email that they owned, like, the hijackers.
sentences.zh: 他们改成了黑客自己控制的邮箱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they changed the security questions.
sentences.zh: 他们还改了安全问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Depending on how, and depending on the specifics of the system.
sentences.zh: 这取决于系统的具体机制。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it can be really bad.
sentences.zh: 但确实，这可能会非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, actually, they do have, so, fortunately, my Gmail account was not hacked because it uses a completely different password.
sentences.zh: 好在我的 Gmail 账号没被黑，因为它用的是完全不同的密码。

sentences.en: But they do have, like, a lot of these websites, like Facebook and Google, have what's called two-factor authentication.
sentences.zh: 但很多网站，比如 Facebook 和 Google，都有所谓的双重身份验证。

sentences.en: And the way this works is you have a program running on your phone, and basically, whenever you have to put in your password to log into, let's say, Gmail,
sentences.zh: 它的工作原理是你在手机上运行一个程序，每当你输入密码登录 Gmail 时，

sentences.en: Gmail, you also have to go on your phone, and you hit a button.
sentences.zh: 你还得打开手机，按下一个按钮。

sentences.en: And the button gives you a six-digit number that you type in along with your password.
sentences.zh: 按钮会给你一个六位数的验证码，你把它和密码一起输入进去。

sentences.en: And so, the idea is for someone to hijack your account, they not only have to have, you know, your password, but they also have to have your phone.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人想劫持你的账号，他们不仅要有你的密码，还得有你的手机。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, that adds another layer of security.
sentences.zh: 这增加了一层安全保障。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Google, I think, actually, well, they have an option to either text you or call you if you don't have a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且 Google 好像还提供短信或电话验证选项，如果你没有智能手机的话。

sentences.en: Oh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 噢，那很酷。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Because I have it set up to call me.
sentences.zh: 因为我设置的是电话验证。

sentences.en: I don't remember why I did that.
sentences.zh: 我不记得为什么要那样设置了。

sentences.en: It's just kind of weird.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点怪怪的。

sentences.en: If I try to log in, my phone will start ringing.
sentences.zh: 如果我尝试登录，手机就会响。

sentences.en: I'm like, why is it ringing?
sentences.zh: 我当时还在想，为什么手机在响？

sentences.en: Oh, wait.
sentences.zh: 噢，等等。

sentences.en: Oh, that's why.
sentences.zh: 噢，原来是这样。

sentences.en: And then it's coming up on screen, like, you know, enter your, I think, what they call it, OTP.
sentences.zh: 然后屏幕上会显示，让你输入所谓的 OTP。

sentences.en: Yeah, one-time password.
sentences.zh: 对，一次性密码。

sentences.en: So, you actually get a call from Google, and it just says, like, three, six, four, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你会接到 Google 的电话，它会报出类似“三、六、四”之类的数字。

sentences.en: And then if you pick up, it's like, this is your Google verification code.
sentences.zh: 接通后它会说：“这是您的 Google 验证码。”

sentences.en: And then they say it once, and then they repeat it.
sentences.zh: 然后它会说一遍，再重复一遍。

sentences.en: That's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那挺酷的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 确实挺酷的。

sentences.en: And I assume texting is probably similar.
sentences.zh: 我想短信验证应该也差不多。

sentences.en: Just text you a six-digit number.
sentences.zh: 就是发给你一个六位数的验证码。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Totally, yeah.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以呢。

sentences.en: I might set up a two-factor authentication on things I really care about so that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我可能会在我真正关心的账号上设置双重身份验证，这样的话，

sentences.en: worst case, if something like this happens and someone gets my password, at least I'm still safe somewhat.
sentences.zh: 最坏的情况下，如果发生了这种事，有人拿到了我的密码，至少我还能保持一定的安全。

sentences.en: Yeah, the only hassle is, and I guess this may be a different controversial subject.
sentences.zh: 是啊，唯一的麻烦是，我想这可能是一个有争议的话题。

sentences.en: Well, maybe not controversial, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许不算有争议，我不知道。

sentences.en: But if you, like, your wife needs access to your email ever.
sentences.zh: 但如果你妻子需要访问你的邮箱时。

sentences.en: So, it was the case where I think we had been communicating with our bank or with somebody, and they had only been using my email for some reason.
sentences.zh: 有一次我们和银行或其他什么人沟通，不知为何他们只用了我的邮箱。

sentences.en: And my wife needed, like, I needed her to print off some documents.
sentences.zh: 我妻子需要打印一些文件。

sentences.en: She was at home and I was at work.
sentences.zh: 她在家里，我在公司。

sentences.en: And so, she needed to get on my email, and she knows my password, but she didn't know my, you know, she couldn't have this code.
sentences.zh: 她需要登录我的邮箱，她知道我的密码，但她拿不到这个验证码。

sentences.en: And so, she had to, like, I had to get the phone call, write the number down, and then call her and give her the number.
sentences.zh: 所以她不得不等我接到电话，记下数字，然后再打电话告诉她。

sentences.en: So, I guess that's really safe, but, you know, it was kind of awkward that, like, I wanted her to be able to have access, but in this way, it was actually difficult to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这确实很安全，但有点尴尬，我本想让她能访问，但用这种方式确实很难。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实。

sentences.en: Maybe, oh, man.
sentences.zh: 也许，天哪。

sentences.en: In hindsight, what I should have done is actually just forward it to her.
sentences.zh: 事后想想，我当时应该直接转发给她。

sentences.en: But, I guess this is controversial as well, but, you know, it's like, you worry about, it's okay for me to do two-step authentication,
sentences.zh: 不过，这可能也有争议，但你会担心，我做双重验证没问题，

sentences.en: and I want to be really safe and have secure passwords, and I, you know, try to educate other people the same way.
sentences.zh: 我想确保安全并使用强密码，我也尝试教别人这样做。

sentences.en: But, you know, you don't always know, and so, there's this hesitancy to, like, you know, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但你并不总是了解情况，所以会有一种犹豫，我不知道。

sentences.en: You don't know what other people's passwords are.
sentences.zh: 你不知道别人的密码是什么样的。

sentences.en: You don't know if they're good, you know, so you don't want to forward something to somebody who might have a, that may be very personal to you or have, you know,
sentences.zh: 你不知道他们是否设置得当，所以你不想把可能涉及个人隐私的信息转发给那些安全意识没那么强的人。

sentences.en: private information, and then they don't have security like you would want.
sentences.zh: 他们没有你想要的那些安全措施。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是啊，完全同意。

sentences.en: So, actually, this, so the big thing to take away from here, folks at home, is, you know, because I'm pretty sure that what happened was, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，各位听众，这里最大的教训是，因为我敢肯定当时的情况是，

sentences.en: I put my password in on some forum, and somebody wasn't, you know, wasn't hashing the passwords, and it just totally got leaked out.
sentences.zh: 我在某个论坛输入了密码，而那个网站没有对密码进行哈希处理，导致密码完全泄露了。

sentences.en: And I think even major websites like joystick.com had this whole thing where all of the passwords got leaked out, like, in plain text.
sentences.zh: 我想即使是像 joystick.com 这样的大网站，也发生过所有密码以明文形式泄露的事情。

sentences.en: So, if you're going to, you know, have a password which you don't really care about, like, if you need throwaway passwords, use KeePass.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你要设置一个不太在意的密码，比如需要一次性密码，就用 KeePass。

sentences.en: Just to recap what it does, you have this master password.
sentences.zh: 简单回顾一下它的功能，你有一个主密码。

sentences.en: You put it in, and it opens up a program with just a list of passwords, and it can auto-generate passwords.
sentences.zh: 输入它，就能打开一个存有密码列表的程序，它还能自动生成密码。

sentences.en: You can type in passwords.
sentences.zh: 你可以输入密码。

sentences.en: You can just, you know, make up passwords on the fly.
sentences.zh: 你可以随时随地创建密码。

sentences.en: It's sort of like writing your passwords down on, like, a sheet of paper for the ones you don't care about.
sentences.zh: 这就像是把你不在意的那些密码写在纸上一样。

sentences.en: But that sheet of paper is now protected, you know.
sentences.zh: 但那张纸现在是被保护起来的。

sentences.en: It's better than just having it, you know, taped, attached to your monitor or something like that.
sentences.zh: 这总比把密码贴在显示器上要好。

sentences.en: You know, although I've actually heard somebody make an argument that it's better to write passwords like that down.
sentences.zh: 虽然我确实听过有人说把密码写下来更好。

sentences.en: So, at least you guarantee they're different, and you aren't encouraged to use the same one over and over again.
sentences.zh: 至少你能保证它们各不相同，也不会被诱导反复使用同一个密码。

sentences.en: Better to do that than...
sentences.zh: 这样做总比……

sentences.en: Than use the same password that's easy or the same.
sentences.zh: 总比使用同一个简单或重复的密码要好。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 噢，是啊。

sentences.en: And, you know, just because that way you can remember it.
sentences.zh: 而且这样你也能记住它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But then, of course, if somebody breaks into your house, they have all your accounts.
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果有人闯进你家，他们就拿到了你所有的账号。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那倒是。

sentences.en: But if someone breaks into your account, into your house, you probably should just change everything.
sentences.zh: 但如果有人闯进你的账号，或者闯进你家，你可能就该把一切都改了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实。

sentences.en: Join the witness protection program.
sentences.zh: 然后加入证人保护计划。

sentences.en: But if, yeah, whether you write them down yourself or whether you use a program like KeePass, use a different password for every website that you don't care about.
sentences.zh: 但无论你是自己写下来还是用 KeePass 这样的程序，对于每一个不在意的网站，都要使用不同的密码。

sentences.en: Because chances are, if you don't care about it, you know, it's probably, they're not, probably not doing a good job securing your password.
sentences.zh: 因为很有可能，如果你不在意那个网站，他们很可能也没做好密码保护工作。

sentences.en: So, don't be like me.
sentences.zh: 所以，别像我一样。

sentences.en: Don't get all your things you don't care about hijacked.
sentences.zh: 别让你那些不在意的账号全被劫持了。

sentences.en: And the bad thing is, you know, since I use the same password for everything I don't care about, then basically, like, all of those things now can be compromised.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的是，因为我所有不在意的账号都用同一个密码，所以基本上，现在所有这些账号都可能被攻破了。

sentences.en: I mean, like, you know, by their nature, I don't care about any of them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从本质上讲，我并不在意它们中的任何一个。

sentences.en: But still, I don't like the idea that someone's going on, like, the MAME arcade forums masquerading as me or whatever, you know?
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我也不喜欢有人在 MAME 街机论坛上冒充我之类的，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Although, I guess that's maybe the least bad thing.
sentences.zh: 虽然我想这可能是最不糟糕的情况了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it's still kind of bad.
sentences.zh: 但确实，这还是挺糟糕的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of a catch-22.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是一个“第 22 条军规”式的困境。

sentences.en: It's like, if I cared enough, I would have put a real password.
sentences.zh: 就像是，如果我足够在意，我就会设置一个真正的密码。

sentences.en: But then, at the same time, like, I don't want somebody, like, masquerading as me.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我又不希望有人冒充我。

sentences.en: Well, it's hard, too, because, like, each individual one you might not have cared enough about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也很难，因为每一个账号你可能都没那么在意。

sentences.en: But now that, like you said, somebody can masquerade as you on many things, that's actually more annoying.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，现在有人可以在很多平台上冒充你，这确实更烦人。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是这样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, all right.
sentences.zh: 好，没问题。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: For the first news story, I had one in here about, and we talked about this a little bit before, about next generation consoles having this, you know, much more kind of a valve,
sentences.zh: 关于第一条新闻，我这里有一则，我们之前稍微聊过一点，是关于下一代游戏主机将采用这种，你知道，更像阀门一样的，

sentences.en: type system where things are more downloaded, and you put in unique keys, and that key is tied to your console or your login, and so you can't, you know,

sentences.en: Also, it has this cool mode where, if you haven't edited a file, it has this, like, the tab on the far left.

sentences.en: So, it uses tabs, like most IDEs, where you have, like, one tab for each file.

sentences.en: But they have one tab, which is, like, all the files that, like, you haven't really edited yet.

sentences.en: And so, like, if you want to look through all your files, it won't create a bunch of tabs like Eclipse will, you know?

sentences.en: And then, if you actually want a file to sort of be sticky, to be a tab, you double-click on it.

sentences.en: So, a lot of times, you're trying to move really fast from, like, the top to the bottom of a file.

sentences.en: So, what about your tool of the buy week?

sentences.en: Like, getting off of my extended stay on non-open source things, I'm finally back onto an open source project.
sentences.zh: 从我长期使用的非开源软件中跳出来，我终于又回到了开源项目。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: Yay.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: And this one is a camera application called Luminance HDR, which stands for High Dynamic Range.
sentences.zh: 这次是一个叫 Luminance HDR 的相机应用，HDR 代表高动态范围。

sentences.en: Or at least that's what it means in camera.
sentences.zh: 至少在摄影领域是这个意思。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: I hope specifically that's what it means in this app.
sentences.zh: 我希望在这个应用里它特指这个意思。

sentences.en: Looks like that.
sentences.zh: 看起来是这样。

sentences.en: And we have a link in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目说明里放了链接。

sentences.en: And so, this is basically, so the idea of a high dynamic range photo in the photography world is that if you take a picture, your camera does basically, it tries to guess, like,
sentences.zh: 简单来说，摄影界中高动态范围照片的概念是，当你拍照时，相机基本上会尝试猜测，比如，

sentences.en: how bright the picture should be.
sentences.zh: 照片应该有多亮。

sentences.en: So, it wants the average brightness of the whole image.
sentences.zh: 它想要的是整个图像的平均亮度。

sentences.en: And this gets a little bit into image processing.
sentences.zh: 这涉及到一点图像处理知识。

sentences.en: But through either mechanical or electrical means or electronic programming means, it tries to determine, like, the average.
sentences.zh: 但通过机械、电气或电子编程手段，它会尝试确定这个平均值。

sentences.en: If you think about, like, a piece of white paper, if that was the only thing on your screen, it kind of tries to make that, like, the middle of white.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一张白纸，如果屏幕上只有它，它会尝试让它处于白色的中间值。

sentences.en: Like, kind of gray.
sentences.zh: 比如，灰色的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, kind of in the middle so that things to the top and bottom don't get washed out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，处于中间位置，这样高光和阴影部分就不会过曝或欠曝。

sentences.en: Like, that's what it wants to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是它想做的。

sentences.en: So, if you think about taking a picture with the bright sky in the background, but, like, I'm taking a picture of Jason in the foreground in the shade.
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下，背景是明亮的天空，而我正在给阴影里的 Jason 拍照。

sentences.en: Sometimes, like, how do you do that?
sentences.zh: 有时候，这该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Because the problem is you can only show so many bits, so much range in your image.
sentences.zh: 因为问题在于，图像中能显示的位数和范围是有限的。

sentences.en: And the fact that I can show the dark of Jason in the shade and the bright of the sunlight, that's easy.
sentences.zh: 我能同时拍出阴影中 Jason 的暗部和阳光下的亮部，这很容易。

sentences.en: But I want to both be able to see the details of Jason in the shade and also see that there's clouds in the sky.
sentences.zh: 但我既想看清阴影中 Jason 的细节，又想看到天空中的云彩。

sentences.en: But really, the camera can only do one or the other.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，相机一次只能做到其中之一。

sentences.en: It can only show the details on Jason or show the clouds in the sky.
sentences.zh: 它要么只能显示 Jason 的细节，要么只能显示天空中的云彩。

sentences.en: I'm sure everyone's had this before where, you know, there's a sun in the background.
sentences.zh: 我相信每个人都遇到过这种情况，背景里有太阳。

sentences.en: They try and take a picture of somebody and the person comes out, like, completely black.
sentences.zh: 他们试图给某人拍照，结果那个人拍出来完全是黑的。

sentences.en: Like, you just get their silhouette.
sentences.zh: 就像只拍到了剪影一样。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a great example.
sentences.zh: 噢，那是个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Or you try to take a picture of something and the sky is all washed out and glowy.
sentences.zh: 或者你试图拍某样东西，结果天空完全过曝，一片惨白。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, okay, so those are kind of the two options it takes, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，这基本上就是它能做的两种选择，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, the limitation isn't really that the camera can't do either.
sentences.zh: 其实限制不在于相机做不到，

sentences.en: It's just it can't do them at the same, or it can't do both.
sentences.zh: 而是它不能同时做到这两点。

sentences.en: It just can't do them at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它就是无法同时兼顾。

sentences.en: And so what HDR is about is taking the one where the foreground that's, well, it doesn't matter,
sentences.zh: 所以 HDR 的做法是，取一张针对暗部拍摄且暗部效果好的照片，

sentences.en: but the area that's dark and looks good when you take an image just for the dark area
sentences.zh: 无论如何，

sentences.en: and combining that with an image that is just of the bright area, but the dark area looks terrible.
sentences.zh: 然后将其与一张针对亮部拍摄但暗部效果很差的照片结合起来。

sentences.en: And you take both of those and kind of smash them together, right?
sentences.zh: 你把这两张照片合在一起，对吧？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And so what the computer can do is use more bits of resolution for that range.
sentences.zh: 计算机可以利用更多的位分辨率来处理这个范围。

sentences.en: So it can, instead of using an 8-bit number to represent the amount of blue in the image, it can use a 16-bit number to represent the amount of blue.
sentences.zh: 所以，它可以用 16 位数字来表示蓝色，而不是用 8 位数字。

sentences.en: But your screen can't display that, and your eye can actually do a better job.
sentences.zh: 但你的屏幕显示不出来，虽然人眼其实能分辨得更好。

sentences.en: But if the screen can't display it, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 如果屏幕显示不出来，那也没用。

sentences.en: And so what it does is use various algorithms to try to show both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以它会使用各种算法，试图同时显示这两者。

sentences.en: So kind of like, I don't care about the middle.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我不在乎中间值。

sentences.en: So squeeze in the bottom and squeeze in the top and kind of ditch the middle.
sentences.zh: 压缩暗部，压缩亮部，舍弃中间部分。

sentences.en: Or just other things by combining those two images.
sentences.zh: 或者通过结合这两张照片来实现其他效果。

sentences.en: But the problem is when you take two images, you don't take them in exactly the same way if you're hand-holding it.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，如果你手持拍摄，拍两张照片时位置不可能完全一样。

sentences.en: They move slightly.
sentences.zh: 它们会轻微移动。

sentences.en: So you also have to shift the images so they are exactly the same on top of each other.
sentences.zh: 所以你还得平移图像，让它们完全重合。

sentences.en: You get all sorts of bad things happen.
sentences.zh: 否则会出现各种糟糕的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's called registering the images.
sentences.zh: 是的，这叫图像对齐。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when you have things that are misaligned, you get ghosting.
sentences.zh: 当图像未对齐时，就会出现重影。

sentences.en: So if a person is walking across the scene, you get ghosting.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人走过画面，就会产生重影。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay, but long story short, this software does that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，长话短说，这个软件就是干这个的。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: And it does it in a way with many, many different options, all sorts of different algorithms, all sorts of thresholds.
sentences.zh: 它提供了非常多的选项、各种不同的算法和各种阈值。

sentences.en: The user interface leaves something to be desired.
sentences.zh: 用户界面还有待改进。

sentences.en: It's not always obvious what you should do.
sentences.zh: 你该怎么做并不总是显而易见的。

sentences.en: And there are pay packages that do a really professional job of this.
sentences.zh: 市面上也有收费软件能非常专业地完成这项工作。

sentences.en: And once you know what an HDR image looks like, a really famous person is Trey Ratcliffe.
sentences.zh: 一旦你知道 HDR 图像是什么样，就会想起一位名人 Trey Ratcliffe。

sentences.en: He's an online personality.
sentences.zh: 他是一位网络红人。

sentences.en: And he takes a lot of HDR images using very expensive, very nice software.
sentences.zh: 他使用非常昂贵、非常好的软件拍摄了大量 HDR 图像。

sentences.en: But if you want to try it out yourself by, you know, kind of doing this example thing, there's a great way to do it with the software.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想自己尝试一下，通过这种示例方式，这个软件是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: And it really teaches you a lot about how it is actually being done as opposed to just doing it all for you, which is bad and good.
sentences.zh: 它能让你真正学到 HDR 是如何实现的，而不是直接帮你全自动完成，这有好有坏。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's totally awesome.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它真的很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, the great thing about this is that, as you said, it's free and open source.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它最棒的地方在于，正如你所说，它是免费开源的。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's nothing stopping someone from giving this a shot and learning something.
sentences.zh: 所以，没什么能阻止你去尝试并学到一些东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I would encourage you to, if you're into photography or even if you're not just interested in image processing, check it out.
sentences.zh: 所以我鼓励你，如果你对摄影感兴趣，或者即使你只是对图像处理感兴趣，也去看看它。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So let's go into the programming language.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈编程语言。

sentences.en: We've sort of ranted for a while, so we'll try to be a little terse.
sentences.zh: 我们已经唠叨了一会儿了，所以我们尽量简短点。

sentences.en: But we're going to talk about IDLs, which is something, interface description languages, which is something I'm really excited about.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈谈 IDL，即接口描述语言，这是我非常感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: I've only been using IDLs for like a little over a year now, but it's really helped my productivity tremendously to the point now where I use it no matter,
sentences.zh: 我使用 IDL 才一年多，但它极大地提高了我的工作效率，以至于现在无论做什么，

sentences.en: even for personal projects, hobbies.
sentences.zh: 即使是个人项目或爱好，我都会用到它。

sentences.en: I almost start with the IDL programming first and then get into, you know, the rest of what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 我几乎都是先从 IDL 编程开始，然后再进行后续的工作。

sentences.en: So from a software engineering standpoint, I mean, interfaces, you kind of alluded to it, starting with it.
sentences.zh: 从软件工程的角度来看，接口，你刚才也提到了，从接口开始。

sentences.en: It's not so much the interface description language.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是接口描述语言的问题。

sentences.en: We'll just say IDL from now on.
sentences.zh: 我们以后就简称它为 IDL。

sentences.en: The IDL is the fact that it's the interface.
sentences.zh: IDL 的核心在于它定义了接口。

sentences.en: Interface is the thing that glues all the parts of your project together.
sentences.zh: 接口是将项目各部分粘合在一起的东西。

sentences.en: If you're using a library, how you interface with that library is very key.
sentences.zh: 如果你在使用一个库，你如何与该库交互至关重要。

sentences.en: If you're going to interface to somebody else, that's like if you define those interfaces first, everything else somewhat falls into place.
sentences.zh: 如果你要与他人对接，如果你先定义好这些接口，其他一切都会顺理成章。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if you think about, you know, if you, you know, although it says interface description language, this is sort of, it's sort of more general than that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想一下，虽然它叫接口描述语言，但这其实更通用一些。

sentences.en: It's also, a lot of these are also sort of data description languages.
sentences.zh: 其中很多其实也是数据描述语言。

sentences.en: And many programs that we write nowadays are sort of data driven.
sentences.zh: 我们现在编写的许多程序都是数据驱动的。

sentences.en: You know, the algorithms and the processes aren't necessarily new or interesting or difficult, but it's just the data.
sentences.zh: 你知道，算法和流程不一定新颖、有趣或困难，关键在于数据。

sentences.en: So, you know, for example, like Instagram or something like that, you know, picture taking had been around forever.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如 Instagram 之类的，拍照功能早就存在了。

sentences.en: But the way that they manipulate the data with the social network and sharing with your friends and things like that is, well, one of the things that makes that product great.
sentences.zh: 但他们处理数据的方式，结合社交网络和好友分享等功能，是让该产品大获成功的原因之一。

sentences.en: But, you know, starting with the IDL lets you sort of lay out a framework for sort of how your program is going to flow, not only in terms of processes and interfaces,
sentences.zh: 所以，从 IDL 开始，可以让你为程序的运行流程搭建一个框架，不仅是在流程和接口方面，

sentences.en: but in terms of the data and what's going to be stored and how.
sentences.zh: 还在于数据以及如何存储数据。

sentences.en: So that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: And we should point out here, people might be saying, well, why do I need a language for that?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里应该指出，人们可能会说，好吧，我为什么需要一种语言来做这件事呢？

sentences.en: And if you're only working on one process on one computer, you might be right.
sentences.zh: 如果你只在一台计算机上处理一个进程，你可能是对的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But these days, like Jason alluded to, even simple applications need to talk to another application or need to talk to another process or go over the network.
sentences.zh: 但如今，正如 Jason 所提到的，即使是简单的应用程序也需要与另一个应用程序通信，或者需要与另一个进程通信，亦或是通过网络进行交互。

sentences.en: And when you do that, you need a way to tell the person on the other end who may be running on a different kind of computer, a different operating system, a different language.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，你需要一种方法来告诉另一端的人，他们可能运行在不同类型的计算机、不同的操作系统或使用不同的语言上。

sentences.en: And you need a way to tell them what your data looks like.
sentences.zh: 而且你需要一种方法来告诉他们你的数据是什么样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, or even if you're talking to disk, you know, if you want to save data to the hard drive, you don't really want to have, yeah, serialize it or marshal it.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你是在与磁盘通信，你知道，如果你想把数据保存到硬盘上，你其实并不想手动去序列化或编组它。

sentences.en: You don't want to have to do that by hand.
sentences.zh: 你不想必须手动完成这些工作。

sentences.en: You know, you want something that is going to generate that for you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你想要一些能为你生成这些代码的东西。

sentences.en: So, yeah, IDLs, how did they start?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，IDL（接口定义语言）是怎么开始的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, there's some classic ones that you hear a lot about, Korba, common object, oh, I'm messing it up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一些你经常听到的经典语言，比如 CORBA，通用对象……噢，我把它搞砸了。

sentences.en: The common object request broker architecture.
sentences.zh: 通用对象请求代理架构（Common Object Request Broker Architecture）。

sentences.en: This is a classic one that's been around for a while.
sentences.zh: 这是一个已经存在一段时间的经典架构。

sentences.en: You hear a lot about.
sentences.zh: 你经常会听到它。

sentences.en: Another one that people might be familiar with if you program on Windows is the common object model that Microsoft uses com for a lot of communicating with its APIs and stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果你在 Windows 上编程，人们可能熟悉的另一种架构是微软使用的组件对象模型（COM），它常用于与 API 等进行通信。

sentences.en: And it's a way to describe how that data should be and what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 这是一种描述数据应该是什么样以及它看起来是什么样的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So, another one is ICE.
sentences.zh: 所以，另一个是 ICE。

sentences.en: That's made by the Zero-G.
sentences.zh: 那是 Zero-G 制作的。

sentences.en: ICE is very similar to Korba.
sentences.zh: ICE 和 CORBA 非常相似。

sentences.en: It came out around the same time under the mantra of, like, we're not as complicated as Korba.
sentences.zh: 它大约在同一时间出现，其口号是，我们不像 CORBA 那么复杂。

sentences.en: But it does functionally the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但它在功能上做着同样的事情。

sentences.en: So, what are some of the ones that we may have heard of more recently?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们最近可能听说过哪些呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, that was the beginning was Korba and ICE, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是 CORBA 和 ICE 等事物的开端。

sentences.en: Then they moved on to sort of the early web era.
sentences.zh: 然后它们进入了早期的 Web 时代。

sentences.en: There was SOAP and JSON RPC.
sentences.zh: 出现了 SOAP 和 JSON RPC。

sentences.en: So, basically, the way these two work is, you know, at the time, you know, there was an XML and a JSON reader and writer in most modern languages.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，这两种工作方式是，在当时，大多数现代语言中都有 XML 和 JSON 的读取器和写入器。

sentences.en: So, they said that this sort of could be an intermediary.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们说这可以作为一种中间媒介。

sentences.en: So, since, you know, Python can write XML and C++ can read XML, we should create some data format.
sentences.zh: 因此，既然 Python 可以编写 XML，而 C++ 可以读取 XML，我们应该创建某种数据格式。

sentences.en: So, you could think of, like, a simple way to do something like SOAP is, let's just have an XML file.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以认为，做类似 SOAP 的事情的一种简单方法是，我们只用一个 XML 文件。

sentences.en: And if you have, like, a class, like a C++ class or a Python class, you just have a tag called class and attribute called name with the class name.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个类，比如 C++ 类或 Python 类，你只需要一个名为 class 的标签，以及一个名为 name 的属性，属性值就是类名。

sentences.en: And then inside of class, you could have many XML tags for all of the members of the class.
sentences.zh: 然后在 class 内部，你可以为类的所有成员设置许多 XML 标签。

sentences.en: And the tag could say, you know, you know, member would be the tag name.
sentences.zh: 标签可以写成 member，这就是标签名。

sentences.en: And then the type, there would be a type attribute saying whether it's, like, a double or a float or an integer or a character.
sentences.zh: 然后是类型，会有一个 type 属性，说明它是双精度浮点数、浮点数、整数还是字符。

sentences.en: And then inside of the member tag, you could actually put the data.
sentences.zh: 然后在 member 标签内部，你实际上可以放入数据。

sentences.en: So, you could actually hold class instances as well as the definitions.
sentences.zh: 所以，你实际上既可以保存类实例，也可以保存定义。

sentences.en: So, that's one way to do SOAP.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是 SOAP 的一种方式。

sentences.en: SOAP is one implementation of that.
sentences.zh: SOAP 是其中的一种实现。

sentences.en: So, for example, a C++ program can write out some classes using this XML format.
sentences.zh: 例如，C++ 程序可以使用这种 XML 格式写出一些类。

sentences.en: And then a Python program could read this XML and then reinterpret it as Python classes.
sentences.zh: 然后 Python 程序可以读取这个 XML，并将其重新解释为 Python 类。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, maybe an example.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许举个例子。

sentences.en: I think we're getting a little bogged down in acronym phobia or acronym, too many acronyms flying around.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们有点陷入了缩写恐惧症，或者说周围充斥着太多的缩写了。

sentences.en: So, like, let's say Jason runs a service that shares pictures with the world or my friends.
sentences.zh: 所以，假设 Jason 运行着一个与世界或我的朋友分享照片的服务。

sentences.en: And I am an application that runs on somebody's computer that wants to upload pictures to Jason.
sentences.zh: 而我是一个运行在某人计算机上的应用程序，想要上传照片给 Jason。

sentences.en: So, an RPC is a remote procedure call.
sentences.zh: 所以，RPC 是远程过程调用（Remote Procedure Call）。

sentences.en: Basically, it's saying, like, I want to be able to initially take a picture that's on my hard drive and send information about, like, who the user is, when the picture was taken,
sentences.zh: 基本上，它是在说，我想能够最初获取硬盘上的一张照片，并发送关于用户是谁、照片是什么时候拍摄的信息，

sentences.en: the picture itself.
sentences.zh: 以及照片本身。

sentences.en: Like, that data I want to send to Jason's web service so that he can then, you know, show it to the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 就像，我想把那些数据发送到 Jason 的 Web 服务，这样他就可以把它展示给全世界。

sentences.en: So, like, how I call a function on his computer to say, oh, here, I want you to upload picture and here's the data.
sentences.zh: 所以，我如何在他的计算机上调用一个函数来说，噢，给你，我想要你上传照片，这是数据。

sentences.en: That's kind of the process that this stuff describes.
sentences.zh: 这正是这些东西所描述的过程。

sentences.en: And then also the reverse.
sentences.zh: 然后反过来也是一样。

sentences.en: Like, later, I might want to pull down that image.
sentences.zh: 比如，稍后，我可能想把那张图片拉下来。

sentences.en: So, I might want to make a call and say, hey, give me image number one.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能想打个电话说，嘿，给我第一张图片。

sentences.en: And then have it give it to me or give me a list of all the images.
sentences.zh: 然后让他把它给我，或者给我所有图片的列表。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And so, then, now, more modern IDLs are sophisticated enough to where they'll actually generate the code for you for many different languages.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在，更现代的 IDL 已经足够复杂，它们实际上可以为你生成多种不同语言的代码。

sentences.en: So, one of them is protocol buffers.
sentences.zh: 所以，其中之一是 Protocol Buffers。

sentences.en: And so, what you can actually do, protocol buffers comes with a compiler.
sentences.zh: 你可以做的是，Protocol Buffers 自带一个编译器。

sentences.en: So, you write your proto file and the proto file will say, oh, I have a message, you know, picture, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你编写你的 proto 文件，proto 文件会说，噢，我有一个消息，比如 picture，对吧？

sentences.en: And picture has a string called name and then it also has, you know, a list of bytes called data, right?
sentences.zh: 然后 picture 有一个名为 name 的字符串，还有一个名为 data 的字节列表，对吧？

sentences.en: Now, you can run the C++ proto generator and it'll generate a bunch of C++ code that can read and write these picture messages.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以运行 C++ proto 生成器，它会生成一堆可以读取和写入这些 picture 消息的 C++ 代码。

sentences.en: Yeah, class.
sentences.zh: 是的，类。

sentences.en: It'll generate a whole class with gets and sets for you.
sentences.zh: 它会为你生成一个带有 getter 和 setter 的完整类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, it'll have a get data, set data.
sentences.zh: 所以，它会有 get data 和 set data。

sentences.en: It'll have a constructor where you can construct new pictures.
sentences.zh: 它会有一个构造函数，你可以用它来构造新的图片。

sentences.en: And then, you can also generate Java code.
sentences.zh: 然后，你也可以生成 Java 代码。

sentences.en: You can generate JavaScript code.
sentences.zh: 你可以生成 JavaScript 代码。

sentences.en: You can generate, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你可以生成等等等等。

sentences.en: In addition to the generator that generates this code, the protocol buffers also comes with a way to serialize.
sentences.zh: 除了生成此代码的生成器之外，Protocol Buffers 还提供了一种序列化的方法。

sentences.en: So, for example, a way to convert it to, like, a binary representation.
sentences.zh: 例如，一种将其转换为二进制表示的方法。

sentences.en: So, there might be some code for each language, like some C++ code, some Java code, which will say, hey, take this message, which, you know, is a class, as Patrick mentioned,
sentences.zh: 所以，每种语言可能都有一些代码，比如一些 C++ 代码，一些 Java 代码，它们会说，嘿，获取这个消息，也就是 Patrick 提到的那个类，

sentences.en: and turn it into a set of bytes that can go into, like, a text file or go across the wire.
sentences.zh: 并将其转换为一组可以进入文本文件或通过网络传输的字节。

sentences.en: And then, also, it says, here's a set of bytes that I created or that someone else created using protocol buffers.
sentences.zh: 然后，它还说，这是我创建的，或者其他人使用 Protocol Buffers 创建的一组字节。

sentences.en: Turn it into the class.
sentences.zh: 把它转换成类。

sentences.en: Yeah, and kind of in that step, too, which is a big gotcha of doing this on your own,
sentences.zh: 是的，在这一步中，这也是你自己做这件事的一个大坑，

sentences.en: is validating that what you got is actually a real class or is the thing that you meant it to be.
sentences.zh: 就是验证你得到的东西是否真的是一个真正的类，或者是否是你想要的东西。

sentences.en: Right, right, and also handling, you know, if the protocol definition, if the proto changes, you know, dealing with that is also, like,
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，还有处理，你知道，如果协议定义，如果 proto 发生了变化，你知道，处理这些问题也像，

sentences.en: brings a whole host of problems that you don't want to have to solve on your own.
sentences.zh: 会带来一大堆你不想自己解决的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, if you've ever, you know, written a class and then written all these getters and setters and thought to yourself, like,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，如果你曾经写过一个类，然后写了所有这些 getter 和 setter，并对自己说，

sentences.en: there should be a way to do this automatically.
sentences.zh: 应该有一种方法可以自动完成这个工作。

sentences.en: Well, you know, that's exactly what, you know, these type of modern IDLs do, is if you separate, as long as you can separate the logic from the data,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这正是这些现代 IDL 所做的，只要你能将逻辑与数据分离，

sentences.en: then you can do this and not really have to ever write getters or setters or serialization or any of that.
sentences.zh: 那么你就可以做到这一点，而不必真正去写 getter、setter、序列化或任何类似的东西。

sentences.en: It's all just done for you.
sentences.zh: 这一切都为你完成了。

sentences.en: And so, most modern programming nowadays,
sentences.zh: 所以，如今大多数现代编程，

sentences.en: you have these sort of container classes that just have a lot of data but can't actually do anything that are just auto-generated from some small proto file or thrift file,
sentences.zh: 你拥有这些容器类，它们只包含大量数据，但实际上什么也做不了，它们只是从一些小的 proto 文件或 thrift 文件自动生成的，

sentences.en: which we'll get into later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讲到这些。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you have a set of handler classes that don't have any data or just have, like,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，你有一组处理类，它们没有任何数据，或者只有少量数据，

sentences.en: a small amount of data but just manipulate these bigger container classes and send them across the wire, write them to a database, etc., etc.
sentences.zh: 但只是操作这些更大的容器类，并将它们通过网络发送，写入数据库等等。

sentences.en: Another modern IDL, and my personal favorite, is Apache Thrift.
sentences.zh: 另一个现代 IDL，也是我个人的最爱，是 Apache Thrift。

sentences.en: So, actually, this was started from the people who made protocol buffers, and you can think of this as sort of like a version 2 of protobuffers.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，这是由制作 Protocol Buffers 的人发起的，你可以把它看作是 Protocol Buffers 的 2.0 版本。

sentences.en: But basically, Thrift adds support for things like lists and sets and maps, the kind of things that, you know, people who have done Java or Python,
sentences.zh: 但基本上，Thrift 增加了对列表、集合和映射的支持，这些东西，你知道，做过 Java 或 Python 的人，

sentences.en: who are familiar with lists or dictionaries in Python.
sentences.zh: 熟悉 Python 中的列表或字典的人。

sentences.en: Apache Thrift has native support for that.
sentences.zh: Apache Thrift 对此有原生支持。

sentences.en: So, in Thrift, for example, you can say, like, I have this Thrift message, and the message is gallery.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 Thrift 中，例如，你可以说，我有这个 Thrift 消息，消息是 gallery。

sentences.en: And my gallery has, let's say, a name, which is, you know, the name of the gallery, maybe an integer, which is the ID for, you know, looking it up later.
sentences.zh: 我的 gallery 有一个名字，也就是 gallery 的名字，可能还有一个整数，它是用于稍后查找的 ID。

sentences.en: And then the third could be a map, which maps strings to picture objects.
sentences.zh: 然后第三个可以是一个映射，将字符串映射到图片对象。

sentences.en: And so, you can map, like, the name of a picture to the actual data.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以将图片的名字映射到实际的数据。

sentences.en: And all this is done in Thrift using just a few lines of this Thrift code.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是在 Thrift 中使用几行 Thrift 代码完成的。

sentences.en: And then you can auto-generate that, you know, class in any language you want.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以用你想要的任何语言自动生成那个类。

sentences.en: I think there's like 15 languages that are supported.
sentences.zh: 我想有 15 种语言支持它。

sentences.en: So, oh, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 所以，噢，请继续。

sentences.en: No, no, yeah.
sentences.zh: 不，不，是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, yeah, there's a lot of choices here.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，是的，这里有很多选择。

sentences.en: It's one of those things when you, I don't remember ever really talking about most of these in school.
sentences.zh: 这是那种当你……我不记得在学校里真正谈论过其中大多数内容。

sentences.en: It's kind of something you learn when you get out in the real world and you start running across these recurring problems of, man, I really need to talk to something else.
sentences.zh: 这有点像当你进入现实世界，开始遇到这些反复出现的问题时学到的东西，天哪，我真的需要和别的东西通信。

sentences.en: And I need to come up with a common way to represent it.
sentences.zh: 我需要想出一个通用的方式来表示它。

sentences.en: And I'm going to roll my own.
sentences.zh: 我要自己动手写一个。

sentences.en: And then you run into a whole bunch of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 然后你会遇到一大堆问题。

sentences.en: So, it's much better to use one of these.
sentences.zh: 所以，使用其中一种工具要好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, just to put it in perspective.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，为了说明问题。

sentences.en: So, one thing that I did sort of early on in my career is we wanted to write a bunch of logging data of sort of like what the state of the system was at different points in time.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在职业生涯早期做的一件事是，我们想写一堆日志数据，记录系统在不同时间点的状态。

sentences.en: And we actually, we had a bunch of classes in C++ that we wrote just by using what's called a memcopy or fwrite.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上在 C++ 中写了一堆类，只是通过使用所谓的 memcopy 或 fwrite。

sentences.en: So, we actually just took the class in binary form and just wrote it to the hard drive.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们实际上只是以二进制形式获取类，并将其写入硬盘。

sentences.en: As ones and zeros.
sentences.zh: 作为 1 和 0。

sentences.en: And then on the other end, to read the class, we actually, you know, we had this file that had a bunch of classes in it.
sentences.zh: 然后在另一端，为了读取这个类，我们实际上，你知道，我们有这个包含一堆类的文件。

sentences.en: So, you think, oh, well, I'll just write some program that just, you know, goes the other way and doesn't fread.
sentences.zh: 所以你会想，噢，好吧，我只要写个程序，用相反的方式做，用 fread 读取就行了。

sentences.en: Ah, but the problem is one machine was big Indian and the other machine was little Indian.
sentences.zh: 啊，但问题是一台机器是大端序（Big Endian），另一台机器是小端序（Little Endian）。

sentences.en: And for people who don't know, Indian means, it's kind of like a pun.
sentences.zh: 对于不知道的人来说，Endian 意味着，它有点像双关语。

sentences.en: It's N-D-N.
sentences.zh: 它是 N-D-N。

sentences.en: It's actually spelled E-N-D-I-A-N.
sentences.zh: 它实际上拼写为 E-N-D-I-A-N。

sentences.en: And basically what it means is, let's say you have a short.
sentences.zh: 基本上它的意思是，假设你有一个 short。

sentences.en: So, a short is a 16-bit number, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，short 是一个 16 位数字，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a two-byte number.
sentences.zh: 它是一个双字节数字。

sentences.en: So, the question is, where should the number start?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，数字应该从哪里开始？

sentences.en: Like, if you're writing a number in English, like, let's say you're writing the number 1,000.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你用英语写一个数字，比如，假设你写数字 1,000。

sentences.en: Well, the number, the most significant part of the number is on the left.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个数字，最重要的部分在左边。

sentences.en: Like, the 1 in 1,000.
The biggest part.
sentences.zh: 最大的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, as in the thousands digit.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像千位数字一样。

sentences.en: Or if you have the number, like, 222, the first two is the most significant.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你有数字，比如 222，第一个 2 是最重要的。

sentences.en: Like, that has the 200, the big part of the number.
sentences.zh: 因为它代表 200，是数字的大部分。

sentences.en: If you lost the first two, that would be a big deal.
sentences.zh: 如果你丢失了第一个 2，那将是一件大事。

sentences.en: If you lost the last two, it wouldn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 如果你丢失了最后两个，那真的没关系。

sentences.en: You'd have 220, let's say.
sentences.zh: 比如，你会有 220。

sentences.en: So, that, in the case of computers, there are some computers which are big Indian.
sentences.zh: 所以，在计算机的情况下，有些计算机是大端序的。

sentences.en: And that is where the first byte of a number, say you have a short, that's two bytes.
sentences.zh: 这就是数字的第一个字节，假设你有一个 short，那是两个字节。

sentences.en: The first byte has the most significant bits in it.
sentences.zh: 第一个字节包含最重要的位。

sentences.en: And the second byte has the smaller, the least significant bits.
sentences.zh: 第二个字节包含较小的、最不重要的位。

sentences.en: Some computers are little Indian, which means it's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 有些计算机是小端序的，这意味着它是反过来的。

sentences.en: So, the first byte has the least significant bits, or the numbers that wouldn't really matter if they weren't there, or if they were set to zero.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个字节包含最不重要的位，或者说如果它们不存在，或者如果它们被设置为零，也不会有什么影响的数字。

sentences.en: So, the computer that was reading the data was little Indian, and the computer that was writing it was big Indian.
sentences.zh: 所以，读取数据的计算机是小端序的，而写入数据的计算机是大端序的。

sentences.en: So, all of the numbers were just completely bogus.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有的数字完全是错误的。

sentences.en: Like, all of them were, like, the bits were reversed.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们全部都是，位被反转了。

sentences.en: So, the numbers were, the bytes were reversed.
sentences.zh: 当时那些数字，那些字节的顺序是反的。

sentences.en: The numbers were just garbage.
sentences.zh: 那些数字简直就是乱码。

sentences.en: So, we had to write all of this code.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不编写所有这些代码。

sentences.en: It was just thousands of lines of code to, like, byte swap all of these, you know, classes.
sentences.zh: 那可是几千行代码，就为了，你知道，把所有这些类进行字节交换。

sentences.en: And byte swap all of the members in the classes.
sentences.zh: 还要交换类中所有的成员。

sentences.en: And it just, it took weeks.
sentences.zh: 这真的花了我们好几周时间。

sentences.en: And if we had known about, you know, Apache Thrift or protocol buffers, we would have saved literally weeks, probably months of work.
sentences.zh: 如果我们当时知道 Apache Thrift 或 Protocol Buffers，我们真的能节省几周，甚至几个月的工作量。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Definitely very useful.
sentences.zh: 确实非常有用。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, there are just tons and tons of gotchas when it comes to moving, you know, turning code into data, or turning, you know, the data that lives inside of code into ones
sentences.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，在处理代码转数据，或者把代码里的数据转换成一和零，也就是序列化和编组时，会有数不清的坑。

sentences.en: and zeros, serialization and marshalling.
sentences.zh: 序列化和编组。

sentences.en: And there's just tons and tons that goes into that.
sentences.zh: 这其中涉及的内容实在太多了。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's interesting to learn about, but if you just want to write something to disk, save yourself the trouble and use Apache Thrift.
sentences.zh: 所以，了解这些很有趣，但如果你只是想把东西写到磁盘上，省省力气，直接用 Apache Thrift 吧。

sentences.en: But, you know, so IDLs kind of are, this is different, you know, as opposed to talking to one specific language, you're talking kind of about a group of languages, but they do
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道，接口定义语言（IDL）有点不同，它不是针对某一种特定的语言，而是面向一组语言，但它们确实

sentences.en: share some common features.
sentences.zh: 共享一些共同的特性。

sentences.en: And some of this idea of this, this common idea of, like, the message, the thing that you might want to send or write to disk.
sentences.zh: 还有这种关于“消息”的通用概念，就是你可能想要发送或写入磁盘的东西。

sentences.en: And generating these, you know, all this ancillary helper code that needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 以及生成所有这些必须完成的辅助代码。

sentences.en: And it's really nice that most of these provide utilities or are part of it where they process these message description files and generate code for you.
sentences.zh: 最棒的是，它们大多数都提供了实用工具，或者作为其一部分，能够处理这些消息描述文件并为你生成代码。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The messages are huge.
sentences.zh: 这些消息非常庞大。

sentences.en: Another big part of it is most IDLs support many different protocols.
sentences.zh: 另一个重点是，大多数 IDL 支持多种不同的协议。

sentences.en: So, for example, Apache Thrift supports JSON.
sentences.zh: 例如，Apache Thrift 支持 JSON。

sentences.en: So, you can send it across over the wire as a JSON object.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以通过网络以 JSON 对象的形式发送它。

sentences.en: And that's really useful for web debugging because, you know, a lot of web technology is sort of designed to expect JSON.
sentences.zh: 这对网页调试非常有用，因为很多网页技术都是为了处理 JSON 而设计的。

sentences.en: It can also send data as binary.
sentences.zh: 它也可以以二进制形式发送数据。

sentences.en: So, if you want to write the data to a file on your hard drive that you don't really care
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想把数据写入硬盘上的文件，而你并不在乎

sentences.en: it to be human readable, you could do binary.
sentences.zh: 它是否可读，你可以使用二进制。

sentences.en: Or if you want to store it in a database, you can use binary.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你想把它存储在数据库中，也可以使用二进制。

sentences.en: Also, many of these have what's called a compact binary.
sentences.zh: 此外，其中许多还支持所谓的紧凑二进制格式。

sentences.en: And this is where they do a lot of sort of processor-intensive work to shrink the size down.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们进行大量处理器密集型工作以缩小体积的地方。

sentences.en: So, this can actually have a dramatic effect.
sentences.zh: 这实际上能产生显著的效果。

sentences.en: So, for example, you know, you might reduce your database size by two-thirds by using a compact encoding.
sentences.zh: 例如，通过使用紧凑编码，你可能会将数据库大小减少三分之二。

sentences.en: Which, you know, if you're dealing with gigs and gigs of data, and if you're using something like Amazon Elastic Cloud or something, this could save you a ton of money.
sentences.zh: 如果你处理的是海量数据，并且使用像 Amazon Elastic Cloud 之类的服务，这能为你节省一大笔钱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The nice thing is also that each library kind of typically has code to handle the details of what it's going out as.
sentences.zh: 好的一点是，每个库通常都有处理数据输出细节的代码。

sentences.en: So, if you're serializing it, like Jason said, in one Indian and then reading it back in another, the protocol will actually have to find what that is.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你像 Jason 说的那样，用一种字节序进行序列化，然后用另一种字节序读回，协议实际上会定义该如何处理。

sentences.en: And so, the readers and writers on both sides all have agreed on what that should be and what to expect.
sentences.zh: 因此，双方的读写器都对应该是什么样以及预期是什么达成了一致。

sentences.en: So, you don't have to worry about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你完全不用担心这个问题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, just for example, and I don't know if this is actually how it works,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我不知道它具体是怎么运作的，

sentences.en: but, you know, the Apache Thrift might say, hey, if you're big Indian, then I'll byte swap everything before I send it out.
sentences.zh: 但 Apache Thrift 可能会说，嘿，如果你是大端序，那我在发送之前会把所有内容进行字节交换。

sentences.en: Like, everything will be in little Indian when it's in between computers or on disk.
sentences.zh: 这样，当数据在计算机之间传输或存储在磁盘上时，一切都会变成小端序。

sentences.en: And that way, it's sort of everyone has the same expectation, you know, and you don't have any crazy data.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，大家的预期都是一致的，你就不会遇到乱七八糟的数据问题了。

sentences.en: So, I mean, some of the good, moving on to strengths, some of the good things about these are these,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，谈到优点，这些工具的一些好处在于，

sentences.en: we talked about the automatic code generation, the ability to use whatever language you want,
sentences.zh: 我们刚才提到的自动代码生成，能够使用你想要的任何语言，

sentences.en: whatever kind of computer you want, whatever kind of operating system you want, go across the internet.
sentences.zh: 使用任何类型的计算机，任何操作系统，跨越互联网。

sentences.en: Those are really the, and the time saving, I mean, these are all really good strengths of the IDLs.
sentences.zh: 这些确实是，还有节省时间，这些都是 IDL 非常好的优点。

sentences.en: But what are some of the weaknesses?
sentences.zh: 但缺点是什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there is a certain amount of engineering work that you have to spend.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实需要投入一定的工程量。

sentences.en: I mean, for one thing, you have to learn this technology and everyone using it has to be aware of it.
sentences.zh: 首先，你必须学习这项技术，而且每个使用它的人都必须了解它。

sentences.en: The other thing is that, you know, it's just like using compilers, just like using everything, it's not going to be as efficient as if you did it by hand, you know.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，就像使用编译器或任何工具一样，它不会像你手动编写那样高效。

sentences.en: I mean, this has been the argument since the beginning of time, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个问题从古至今一直都在争论，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, oh, if I wrote assembly by hand, it would be so much better.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，如果我手动写汇编，那肯定会好得多。

sentences.en: But, you know, there are cases, like especially, you know, let's say you want some real-time sensitive,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，有些情况下，特别是，假设你需要一些实时敏感的场景，

sentences.en: like you're writing some plug-in to do video conferencing or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如你在编写一个用于视频会议的插件之类的东西。

sentences.en: You probably want to write your own serialization that takes advantage of certain nuances of your environment.
sentences.zh: 你可能想编写自己的序列化程序，以利用你所处环境的某些细微差别。

sentences.en: So, let's say you're doing sending video, like compressing video.
sentences.zh: 假设你在发送视频，比如压缩视频。

sentences.en: You probably don't want to use Apache Thrift to compress video because video has certain characteristics.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想用 Apache Thrift 来压缩视频，因为视频有其特定的特性。

sentences.en: Like, the human eye cannot really distinguish shades of blue.
sentences.zh: 比如，人眼其实分辨不出蓝色的细微差别。

sentences.en: And you want to take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 你想利用这一点。

sentences.en: You want to compress blue more than everything else.
sentences.zh: 你想比其他颜色更大幅度地压缩蓝色。

sentences.en: These are the kind of things, like, you don't want to use an IDL for.
sentences.zh: 这些就是你不应该使用 IDL 的场景。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And also, I mean, if you're not careful or, like Jason said, if there's potential things that you know more about than the general solution, it can take longer.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你不小心，或者像 Jason 说的，如果你掌握的信息比通用解决方案更多，它反而可能花费更长时间。

sentences.en: If you were going to write a very custom binary format, you might be able to make it smaller than what any of these things are able to do.
sentences.zh: 如果你要编写一个非常定制的二进制格式，你可能能够做得比这些工具所能达到的更小。

sentences.en: So, there might be overhead there that's associated with that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这其中可能存在相关的开销。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: So, some good tools for doing IDLs.
sentences.zh: 那么，介绍一些好用的 IDL 工具。

sentences.en: I use Thrift for Eclipse.
sentences.zh: 我用的是 Eclipse 的 Thrift 插件。

sentences.en: So, basically, it does, like, syntax highlighting and things like that.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它能做语法高亮之类的功能。

sentences.en: I think it can actually run the Thrift code generator for you.
sentences.zh: 我想它甚至可以直接为你运行 Thrift 代码生成器。

sentences.en: So, when you make changes to the Thrift file, it will auto-generate the code.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你修改 Thrift 文件时，它会自动生成代码。

sentences.en: For me, it's easier just to, you know, to run the command that generates the code.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，直接运行生成代码的命令更简单。

sentences.en: It's not that much work.
sentences.zh: 那并不费事。

sentences.en: But I think you can, with some elbow grease, you can set it up to be sort of more streamlined.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，只要花点功夫，你也可以把它设置得更精简。

sentences.en: Another one is, for protocol buffers, is protoclips.
sentences.zh: 另一个针对 Protocol Buffers 的工具是 Protoclips。

sentences.en: And that's very similar, but for that format.
sentences.zh: 它非常相似，只是针对那种格式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, I mean, very useful, very flexible.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，它非常有用，非常灵活。

sentences.en: If you want to talk across the web, do remote procedure calling.
sentences.zh: 如果你想跨网络通信，进行远程过程调用。

sentences.en: If you want to serialize data to disk.
sentences.zh: 如果你想把数据序列化到磁盘。

sentences.en: If you want to just store something.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是想存储一些东西。

sentences.en: Also, some databases, you know, have this language and are able to do kind of more intelligent things
sentences.zh: 此外，一些数据库也支持这种语言，并且能够做一些更智能的事情，

sentences.en: if they know in advance, like, what, like the description of what your data is stored as.
sentences.zh: 如果它们预先知道你的数据存储格式的描述。

sentences.en: Yeah, these are really powerful things.
sentences.zh: 是的，这些功能非常强大。

sentences.en: Something that not everybody knows about.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: They're not completely obvious.
sentences.zh: 它们并不完全显而易见。

sentences.en: But when you learn about them, they're a great, great help.
sentences.zh: 但当你了解它们之后，它们会是极大的助力。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, if you've ever seen something that was sort of transformed to the web.
sentences.zh: 是啊，如果你见过那种被转换到网页上的东西。

sentences.en: Like, I saw recently, like, SSH on the web or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如我最近看到的，网页版 SSH 之类的东西。

sentences.en: Or you see these, like, video games, like, FreeSibs, they ported it to the web.
sentences.zh: 或者你看到这些电子游戏，比如 FreeCiv，他们把它移植到了网页上。

sentences.en: And you figure, like, how is that possible?
sentences.zh: 你会想，这怎么可能？

sentences.en: Like, did they rewrite all of this in JavaScript?
sentences.zh: 他们是用 JavaScript 重写了所有代码吗？

sentences.en: You know, like, how is this running in my browser?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这到底是怎么在我的浏览器里运行的？

sentences.en: Well, chances are the JavaScript is just some thin client.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很有可能 JavaScript 只是一个瘦客户端。

sentences.en: And it's using something like Thrift or protocol buffers to talk to some, you know, bigger program on the server that's running in C++ or Java or whatever.
sentences.zh: 它使用 Thrift 或 Protocol Buffers 之类的东西与服务器上运行的更大的程序进行通信，可能是 C++、Java 或其他语言编写的。

sentences.en: Well, I wanted to point out, well, finishing up with IDLs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想指出的是，关于 IDL 的话题就到此为止。

sentences.en: We have a lot of great user feedback.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了很多很棒的用户反馈。

sentences.en: We, user feedback, listener feedback.
sentences.zh: 我们，用户反馈，听众反馈。

sentences.en: So we've had a great amount of reviews on iTunes.
sentences.zh: 我们在 iTunes 上收到了大量的评论。

sentences.en: Thank you guys for those.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: We've had some good feedback on our Google Plus page.
sentences.zh: 我们在 Google Plus 页面上也收到了一些很好的反馈。

sentences.en: People have given us a lot of show topic ideas that they want to hear about, things they want to talk about, encouragements, some helpful things to watch out for in the future,
sentences.zh: 大家给了我们很多节目主题建议，他们想听的内容，想讨论的话题，鼓励，以及未来需要注意的一些有用的建议，

sentences.en: what people like hearing, what they don't like hearing.
sentences.zh: 大家喜欢听什么，不喜欢听什么。

sentences.en: So we're really appreciative of all that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常感谢所有这些反馈。

sentences.en: It's glad to know you guys are out there and there's other people on the other end of these microphones.
sentences.zh: 很高兴知道你们都在那里，麦克风的另一端还有其他人。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, we have added, like, all of the, you know, requests to our list of programming languages to cover.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们已经把所有的请求都加到了我们的编程语言覆盖列表中。

sentences.en: We want to sort of, like, cover sort of a variety of languages and sort of mix it up between the common ones and some of the more uncommon.
sentences.zh: 我们想涵盖各种各样的语言，在常见的和一些不常见的语言之间进行混合。

sentences.en: But we definitely have taken all the feedback and we're definitely going to keep covering languages until we've gotten every request out the door.
sentences.zh: 但我们绝对已经采纳了所有的反馈，并且一定会继续介绍各种语言，直到我们把所有的请求都完成。

sentences.en: So definitely keep, definitely, and beyond.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要继续，一定要，甚至更多。

sentences.en: So definitely keep sending us your feedback.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要继续给我们发送反馈。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: If you have any particular show topics that you want to cover, like if you're really interested in, like, you know, embedded stuff
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何特别想听的节目主题，比如你对嵌入式开发非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: and you want Patrick to give, like, a little tutorial on how to make, like, an RC car or something.
sentences.zh: 并且希望 Patrick 做一个关于如何制作遥控车之类的简短教程。

sentences.en: Or if you're interested in, like, games or AI or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你对游戏、人工智能或其他任何东西感兴趣。

sentences.en: I mean, if you have any requests or any special topics you want to hear, definitely shoot us a post on the G+.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你有任何请求或任何想听的特别话题，一定要在 G+ 上给我们发帖。

sentences.en: And we'd be happy to respond to that.
sentences.zh: 我们很乐意回应。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, that's a wrap.
sentences.zh: 那么，节目到此结束。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家。
